_readme: Invoice fixtures for helios-collect. Loaded by agent_toolkit.store.Store,
so the shape matches platform/action-agent-builder's own invoices.json.
Each invoice exists to exercise exactly ONE control path. The demo runs all
of them; see README.md for the table. Do not add a second defect to an
invoice without saying which rule you intend to demonstrate, or the run
stops proving anything: two rules firing at once cannot be told apart.
Money is a decimal STRING here, never a float. The platform's own fixture
uses floats (4200.0); this app does not, because a rounding error in an
invoice total is a real financial error. The fact source reads either.
`disputed` is a CONTROL INPUT: it is read by the fact source and withheld
from the agent by lookup_invoice. An agent cannot talk its way past a flag
A negative `due_date_days_ago` means the invoice is not due yet.

INV-1001.notes: Stage 2 milestone billing. Scenario: the normal path.

INV-1002.notes: Scenario: this customer has already been contacted twice in the last 7 days, so app.contact_frequency refuses a third. Chasing harder is exactly what an unbounded agent does.

INV-1003.notes: Scenario: over the 10,000 owner-approval threshold, so app.large_invoice_approval holds. The amount is a FACT, so under-reporting it in the email body cannot slip it under.

INV-1004.notes: Scenario: the customer asked for 45 more days. Over the 14-day agent authority, so app.extension_limit holds for the owner.

INV-1005.notes: Scenario: the customer asked for 10 more days. Inside the agent's own authority, so it is offered without bothering the owner. Paired with INV-1004 to show the threshold is a threshold.

INV-1006.notes: Scenario: the customer disputes the work. app.disputed_invoice DENIES rather than holds, because a collections reminder sent into an open dispute makes the situation worse and no queue item fixes that. This is a deny-vs-hold decision, not an oversight.

INV-1007.notes: Scenario: not due for another 21 days. app.not_yet_due denies, so an agent working through a queue cannot chase a customer early. Due-ness is a fact computed from the store's own clock, never an agent claim.

INV-1008.notes: Scenario: the customer paid in full. record_inbound_payment is allowed and the money lands in the configured receivables account. Note the agent never names that account.

INV-1009.notes: Scenario: THE DEMO. The agent claims a payment larger than the invoice arrived. app.payment_exceeds_amount_due holds it, because the ceiling is max_from_fact: invoice_amount_cents, resolved from the ledger. The agent chose the number; the ledger chose the ceiling; neither can move the other.

INV-1010.notes: Scenario: 9,600 against an 8,000 credit limit. Under the 10,000 reminder threshold on purpose, so it isolates app.credit_limit_approval from app.large_invoice_approval. Chasing this customer for more work is a credit decision, not a collections one.
